second_order: Playing out the Team Skull takeover
theme_note: These codes share the practice of making the subreddit’s own April Fools takeover happen through characters, catchphrases, art, songs, altered recurring formats, and moderator-operated language. What varies is the part played—grunt, boss, rival, moderator, artist, or ordinary poster adapting a familiar format. This is kept apart from vote-and-reward stunts and from explicit resistance or closure.

second_order: Questioning, resisting, and closing Team Skull day
theme_note: These codes test the takeover’s safety, rules, repetition, truth, and duration, stage counter-revolutions, explain its planning, repair its display, redirect it elsewhere, or end it. Positions vary from accessibility complaints and refusal to affectionate requests that it continue; what holds them together is negotiating the takeover rather than performing its central voice.

second_order: Testing and answering April Fools posts
theme_note: These codes make or answer April Fools posts outside the Team Skull performance: checking the calendar, exposing a last-line gag, rating the effort, replying as a moderator, and redoing art after a bamboozle. They vary from initiating jokes to recognizing and repairing them, and stay separate because the practice does not depend on the takeover identity.

second_order: Calling people to make Pokémon on r/place
theme_note: These codes recruit help, offer coordinates or targets, revise a location, volunteer, and report partial progress on proposed Pokémon, balls, logos, or a Team Skull mark. Some calls are precise and answered while many are isolated; the shared practice is trying to get an image made, not protecting or remembering one.

second_order: Spotting and remembering what the canvas held
theme_note: These codes notice figures, celebrate a return or survival, mourn losses, catalogue sprites and coordinates, claim contributions, correct the list, and explain the finished canvas. They range from live sightings to post-event memory, but all make canvas work visible as something found or recalled rather than launch a new build.

These codes use votes, front-page placement, image-search visibility, threats, or promised rewards to turn attention itself into the joke. The promises range from bans and search manipulation to costumes, giveaways, and impossible gifts; their common practice is soliciting visible participation, not simply speaking as Team Skull.

second_order: Defending and negotiating over canvas pictures
theme_note: These codes answer overwriting, vandalism, crowding, borders, flags, and limited space by restoring, attacking, protecting, seeking permission, scaling down, apologizing, or offering mutual protection. The positions can be hostile or cooperative, but each manages competing claims on pixels rather than merely proposing a new picture.

second_order: Moving canvas planning into a megathread and Discord
theme_note: These codes gather scattered plans and real-time updates in a moderator megathread and Discord, redirect a standalone proposal there, and recruit sprite makers to defend and rebuild together. What varies is whether the hub is announced, enforced, or joined; the common practice is choosing a shared planning room.

second_order: Calling for pixels after r/place ended
theme_note: These codes propose Slowpoke or another image after placement has closed and answer by nearly falling for it, correcting the caller, or recognizing the joke. The initiating calls vary between deliberate joke and belated proposal; the shared practice is making the closed canvas itself the point of the exchange.
